advisor.subscription.disabled.title: Subscription {subscription} is disabled
advisor.subscription.disabled.detail: {has_db, select, true {Subscription {subscription} (database {database})} other {Subscription {subscription}}} is disabled, so it applies no change from its publications ({publications}). {has_slot, select, true {Its slot {slot_name} on the publisher keeps every change it has not confirmed, and the WAL that holds them fills the publisher's disk until the subscription is enabled or the slot dropped.} other {It has no slot (slot_name = NONE), so the publisher keeps nothing for it.}}
advisor.subscription.disabled.remediatio: Find why it was disabled (with disable_on_error, the subscriber's log names the failed change), fix it, then ALTER SUBSCRIPTION {ident} ENABLE;. If it is no longer needed, DROP SUBSCRIPTION {ident}; also drops its slot on the publisher.
advisor.subscription.not_receiving.title: Subscription {subscription} has no apply worker running
advisor.subscription.not_receiving.detai: {has_db, select, true {Subscription {subscription} (database {database})} other {Subscription {subscription}}} is enabled, but no apply worker runs for it, so no change is applied. A worker that fails, on a conflict or a lost connection to the publisher, is restarted after wal_retrieve_retry_interval, and fails again until the cause is fixed.
advisor.subscription.not_receiving.remed: Read the subscriber's log for the apply worker's error. For a conflicting row, fix the row on the subscriber, or skip the transaction with ALTER SUBSCRIPTION {ident} SKIP (lsn = ...) once its changes are known to be unwanted.
advisor.subscription.not_receiving.silen: Subscription {subscription} has heard nothing from its publisher for {silence_long, select, true {{silence}} other {{silence_minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}}}

The apply worker of {has_db, select, true {Subscription {subscription} (database {database})} other {Subscription {subscription}}} last received a message from the publisher at {receipt}. The publisher sends a keepalive at least every half wal_sender_timeout when it has nothing else to send, so the connection is stuck or the publisher's walsender is not running.
Check the publisher's walsender for slot {slot_name} (pg_stat_replication) and the network between the two. ALTER SUBSCRIPTION {ident} DISABLE; then ENABLE; restarts the worker.
advisor.subscription.errors.title: Subscription {subscription} is failing
advisor.subscription.errors.detail: The workers of {has_db, select, true {Subscription {subscription} (database {database})} other {Subscription {subscription}}} failed while {has_apply, select, true {{has_sync, select, true {applying changes and copying tables or sequences} other {applying changes}}} other {copying tables or sequences}} since the previous scrape ({apply_errors} apply and {sync_errors} sync errors in all, since the statistics were last reset); each failure stops the worker until it is restarted.
advisor.subscription.errors.remediation: Read the subscriber's log for the error: most are a row that conflicts with one already on the subscriber, a missing table or column, or a permission the subscription owner lacks.
advisor.logical_slot.spill_high.title: Logical slot {slot} spills decoding to disk
advisor.logical_slot.spill_high.detail: Decoding for slot {slot} writes {spill}/s of transactions to disk, because they outgrow logical_decoding_work_mem before they commit. Spilled changes are written and read back, which slows replication and adds I/O on this server.
advisor.logical_slot.spill_high.remediat: Raise logical_decoding_work_mem (64MB by default; ALTER SYSTEM SET logical_decoding_work_mem = '256MB'; SELECT pg_reload_conf();), or have the subscription stream large transactions (ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... SET (streaming = parallel)).
